subject: maths
question: An iron is bought for ₹ 210. Decide its MRP so that after a discount of 5%, you still gain 90%.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

⇒ 210 times (190)/(100) = MRP times (95)/(100)

⇒ MRP = Rs. 420 

**∴ The MRP is Rs. 420.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__****Given:**

CP = Rs. 210

**Formula used:**

Selling price at profit = Cost price x (100 + profit%)/100

Selling price at discount = Marked Price x (100 - discount%)/100

**Calculation:**

SP for gain 20% = 210 x 190/100

⇒ Rs. 399

According to question,

MRP x 95/100 = 399

⇒ MRP = Rs. 420 

∴ The MRP is Rs. 420.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**Profit = Selling price - Cost price

Profit% = [(Selling price - Cost price) × 100] ÷ Cost price

Selling price at profit = Cost price x (100 + profit%)/100

Loss = Cost price - Selling price

Loss% = [(Cost price - Selling price) × 100] ÷ Cost price

Selling price at loss = Cost price x (100 - loss%)/100

Selling price at discount = Marked Price x (100 - discount%)/100
